title: Source inventory panel
summary: This iteration makes the registered collection surface visible as reader-facing source-first content. It renders all 154 safe public collection entries from `config/sources` after the logical source map and before story sections, groups them by the fixed source display sections, and exposes only public-safe metadata such as kind, enablement, tier, authority, platform, and generic config status.

validation_commands: node --input-type=module -e "import { buildSourceInventoryRows } from './src/source-effectiveness.js'; const rows = buildSourceInventoryRows({ rootDir: process.cwd() }); console.log(rows.length);"
node --test --test-name-pattern "source map scan index|source-first IA dashboard|source-first IA status focus|source inventory panel" tests/unit.test.js
Playwright desktop/mobile visual check for docs/reports/2026/06/2026-06-29.html; screenshots in .tmp/phase6-source-inventory-desktop.png and .tmp/phase6-source-inventory-mobile.png

lessons.lesson: Collection entries and logical sources need separate reader surfaces.
lessons.evidence: The logical source map still summarizes 22 status rows, while the new inventory panel lists 154 registry entries grouped under the same fixed display sections.
lessons.recommended_action: Keep status reasoning on logical sources, and use the inventory panel to show every subscribed or configured collection entry.

lessons.lesson: Public source inventory must avoid leaking configuration internals.
lessons.evidence: The renderer exposes generic config status tokens such as `url`, `manual`, `env_required`, and `kill_switch` instead of URL fields, env var names, keyword filters, notes, audit trails, scores, or debug snapshots.
lessons.recommended_action: When adding collection metadata, only surface fields that are explicitly reader-safe or map them to generic status tokens first.

followups.action: Use the source display handbook to manually tune the fixed importance order, then replay the inventory E2E checks to confirm new source insertions land in the expected section.
